note: The rules the guard checks every test procedure against, beside the facts they cite. Signed with the card: a person who signs it signs these rules too. The guard's code knows none of them; it evaluates what is written here (harness/core/rules.ts).

rules.says: the volume under test is an ISA-95 path, such as /habitat/lab
the device the steps command is an ISA-95 path
a procedure gives its CO2 maximum and abort, its minimum speed and its maximum duration
every step gives its speed and its duration
a procedure may raise the floor, never lower it
the step stops the scrubber: a test never stops the only scrubber of a volume, it does not restart at once
below the floor of a test
below the procedure's own minimum
above full speed
the CO2 abort sits at or under the ceiling of a test
the CO2 maximum sits below the abort
the test would stop at its first reading
the test starts there and has no room to rise
a step lasts
the longest exposure one test may cause
the steps last no longer than the procedure's maximum
every test stops on its CO2 and on a refused command
a condition nobody can read would trip the test at its first minute
the night's reserve for the scrubber
a test that does not say what it expects to see cannot be told from a fishing trip

unread.says: read biomed.presence before submitting: a procedure on a volume whose occupancy was not read is refused

blocked.says: no test exposes a person under a critical health alarm; the test waits until the alarm is cleared or the person is out of the volume (read biomed.presence again)

rules.says: an occupied volume is watched: name every occupant in monitoring.subjects, with the band, and stop the test on their verdict (the medical monitor is on standby until the test is authorised; the station starts it then for the subjects the procedure names)
the monitored band starts at the card's minimum or higher
the monitored band ends at the card's maximum or lower
